dialog.body: City of Newport Utilities, this is Tony. How can I help you this afternoon?

Yes, hello. Um, I'm calling about my water bill. The sewer and water, the whole thing. I have it here and it's, it's higher again. I have you on the speaker, I hope that's okay, my hands are not so good for holding the phone.
Speaker's fine, I can hear you okay. Let me pull up the account. Can I get the name on it?

Well, that's the thing. It's still in my husband's name. Haddad, Karim Haddad. He passed, and nobody ever changed it. I'm Anh, his wife. Anh Haddad. So when I call they always ask me for him, and he can't come to the phone, you know?

Understood, Mrs. Haddad. That's very common, and I'm sorry for your loss. Since you're the one living there and paying it, I can talk with you about the account. What's the service address, so I make sure I've got the right one?
Oh. It is, um, the house. I don't want to say it on the phone, so many people calling. You can find it by his name, no?
I can look it up by the name, sure. Give me a second. [pause] Okay, I've got a Karim Haddad here. Is there a mailing address on the bill, in the top corner?
Yes, but it's the same. Okay, okay. I'll just trust you. You have the one with the, the quarterly bill, yes?
Yes, that's the one I'm looking at. It looks like it's billed every three months. The latest one came out in December. What's the amount you've got in front of you?

It says two hundred, ah, no. Wait. Let me put on my glasses. [pause] Two hundred and eighty-one dollars and something. For three months! For one old lady! Tôi sống một mình, I live alone, sorry, sorry. I live alone, Tony. How do I use that much water?

No need to apologize, go ahead in either language. Let me look at the usage. So the way the bill works, there's a meter reading, and the difference from the last reading is what you used. Then there's the water charge and the sewer charge on top of that, based on that usage.
The sewer, I don't even understand why the sewer is so much. The sewer is the same as the water, nearly. I don't put the water in the sewer, I put it in the, the tomatoes, in summer.

Right, and I hear that a lot. In most cases the sewer charge follows the water that comes through the meter, so whatever goes in, they count it as going out. I can't change that part on my end, but what I can do is see whether the reading itself looks off.
Yes, that's what I want. Because last time it was less. I think it was less. And they told me an estimate, maybe? Was it an estimate?

Let me look. [pause] Okay. The December bill is marked as an actual read, not an estimate. The one before it, in September, that one was an estimate, and it came in lower. So what probably happened is the actual read caught up on what the estimate missed.
Ah. So they guess low, then they bill me for the guess being wrong. That's very convenient for the city. Very nice.
I can see why it feels that way. It's not meant as a trick, but yeah, when an estimate is low, the next real read makes up the difference. It evens out over time.

It doesn't even out for me. I'm on a, a fixed income. Everything is planned. I need to make a budget, you understand? So can you give me the, the month by month? How much water each month. Tháng, each month, I want to write it down.

Sure, I can do that. Bear in mind it's billed quarterly, so I may only have readings for each billing period, not every single month. Let me see what I have. [pause] I've got the last four bills. Do you have a pen?
I have a pen. Go, go. I'm writing on the back of the envelope.

Okay. The bill from December covers about September to early December, and that's the one with the actual read, the two eighty-one. The one before that, the September bill, was the estimate, and it was a good bit lower, around one hundred and sixty.
One sixty. Okay. One sixty. Wait, slowly. [pause] One six zero. Yes.
Then going back, the June bill was around one hundred and ninety, and the March one was about one fifty-five. Those are rounded, but they're close.

One ninety, and one fifty-five. So the summer is more, because of the garden, and then this one is the big one. Hmm. If I do the, the average, it's about one eighty a quarter, so sixty a month. Yes? That is what I should put in my budget?

That's a reasonable way to do it. Add all four and divide, you'd land around a hundred and ninety a quarter, so roughly sixty-five a month. If you want to be safe, put in seventy and you'll have a little cushion.
Seventy. Okay. I don't like cushion, I like to know exactly. But okay. Sorry, I'm a little cross today. It's not you.

No, that's fine, I'd be asking the same thing. And if you'd like, I can put in a request for the meter to be re-read, just to double check that number. If it's right, it's right, but at least you'll know.
Yes. Do that. Please. Because I really think, a hundred and, what, from one sixty to two eighty, it's too big a jump. Maybe the meter is old, like me.

Ha, well, I'll put it in. A tech would check the read and also look for a running toilet or a small leak, since that's a common reason for a jump like this. For that I'll need a number to reach you. Is the one on the account still good?
The account is his number, old one, it doesn't work. Use mine. It's four-oh-one, five five five, zero one nine four.

Got it, four-oh-one, five five five, zero one nine four. And I'll note it's Anh Haddad calling about the account in Karim's name. While we're on that, if you'd like to get the account put in your name, there's a form for it, and we can mail it to you.
Mail it, yes, please. I'm tired of saying his name like he's still... [pause] Anyway. Yes, mail it. It goes to the same house.
Will do. It should be in your mailbox in a few days.

Good. Now, the bill. I want to pay it before the weekend. Because my pension check comes the third of every month, always the third, and this month it already came, so I have the money now. Next month I'm short again, so I want it done.
That makes sense, get it paid while the money's there. When are you hoping to do it?

Well, it's Thursday. It's almost three o'clock. You close at, what, four? Five? I can't walk down there today, my knee. And tomorrow my neighbor drives me to the doctor. So how do I pay when the office is closed? In the evening, or Saturday, Sunday? Is there a box, a telephone, the computer? I don't really do the computer. My granddaughter, no, never mind.

A few options. There's a drop box at City Hall where you can leave a check in an envelope with the bill stub, and that's available outside regular hours. You can also pay online on the city's website anytime with a card or from a bank account. And if you'd rather do it by phone, you can pay with me right now, today, and it posts right away.
By phone, now, with you? Today?
Yes, ma'am, we take cards over the phone during the day. After hours, it's the drop box or the website. The mail works too, but that's slower, so for before the weekend I'd go with today or the box.
The box, I can't get there. Phone today, I'm not ready, my card is in the other room and the speaker, I would have to walk. Can I check? I send a check, or I call you back in one hour?

You've got until we close, so yes, you can call back this afternoon, same number, and ask for utilities. Or if the check is easier, your neighbor could drop it in the box tomorrow while you're at the doctor.
Hm. The neighbor, maybe. He's a good boy, he's sixty. Okay. And the check, I write it to who? And his name, or mine?
Make it out to the City of Newport, and write the account number from the top of your bill on the memo line. The name on the check can be yours, that's fine. Just include the stub if you can.
City of Newport, and the number on the memo. Okay, I'm writing. [pause] Oh, but if the meter man finds something wrong, I already paid. Then what?
Then it comes back as a credit on the next bill. You wouldn't lose it. And the re-read request doesn't hold up the payment or anything, so you won't get a late notice while it's pending.
Good. That I like. No late notice. Because last year I had one and it was, nấu, how do you say, I was boiling. I was so angry.
I bet. Well, I've put a note on the account about the re-read, so it should be on file if anybody looks.
Okay. So, to repeat. Re-read of the meter, you call me on my number. The form for my name comes in the mail. The sixty-five, seventy a month for the budget. And the check in the box, City Hall.
That's all of it. And the website's there anytime if your granddaughter wants to set it up for you later on.
Maybe. We'll see. Thank you, Tony. You explain better than the last one. The last one used big words and I said, speak English, and he did not like it.
Ha, well, glad I could help. Have a good afternoon, Mrs. Haddad, and good luck with the knee.
Yes, yes. Goodbye now. Cảm ơn. Thank you.
